original_value: Health telemonitoring systems are constrained by the computational and data transmission load resulting from the large volumes of various measured signals, e.g. in the fall detection application. Nevertheless, the trend of movement and the implementation of computer intelligence in intelligent devices ensure an intelligent and convenient method for continuous real‐time telemonitoring of health conditions. In this paper, fall detection is presented while leveraging edge computing integrated on a multi‐level architecture combines the Wireless Sensors Network and the Internet of Things. Particularly, we present a complete study and implementation scenarios while investigating the performances of machine learning algorithms to distinguish between different fall patterns and activities of daily living using a set of significant extracted features from measured acceleration and angular velocity signals. For low computational requirements and to improve the classification performances, the Linear Discriminant Analysis is used to reduce the dimensionality of extracted features. The experimental results assess the performances of the proposed approach in fall detection that show the highest accuracy of 99.92% provided using the KNN classifier and accuracy of 97.5% for fall pattern recognition using the SVM classifier. Also, the online classification on the Fog device reached an accuracy of 94.42% using the SVM classifier.

result.paraphrase: Health telemonitoring systems face computational and data-transmission burdens because they process large volumes of diverse measured signals, as in fall detection applications. Even so, advances in movement sensing and embedded intelligence in smart devices provide an intelligent, convenient way to continuously monitor health conditions in real time. This paper presents a fall detection approach based on edge computing within a multilayer architecture that combines Wireless Sensors Networks and the Internet of Things. Specifically, it offers a comprehensive study and implementation scenarios, examining the performance of machine learning algorithms in distinguishing among different fall patterns and activities of daily living using significant features extracted from acceleration and angular velocity measurements. To reduce computational demands and improve classification performance, Linear Discriminant Analysis is applied to lower the dimensionality of the extracted features. Experimental results evaluate the proposed fall-detection method and report a peak accuracy of 99.92% with the KNN classifier, 97.5% accuracy for fall-pattern recognition with the SVM classifier, and 94.42% accuracy for online classification on the Fog device using the SVM classifier.
